text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the specific movements you are experiencing and when they first started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent start on risperidone, have you noticed any involuntary muscle stiffness, tremors, or repetitive movements like grimacing or tongue protrusion? I also need to know if you have any other new medications or substance use that might be contributing to these symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms you describe—inner restlessness and an urge to move—are classic signs of akathisia, a common side effect of antipsychotics like risperidone. To confirm this, do you feel that the pacing and fidgeting provide any temporary relief from that uncomfortable inner sense of restlessness?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the symptoms align with akathisia and you have denied substance use, I will request a physical examination to objectively assess the severity of your restlessness and rule out other movement disorders. REQUEST TEST: Physical_Exam
